title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: RENEE GOES BACK
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Renee Coleman, forty-six, from Huntsville, Alabama.
For twenty-two years, she raised three boys. Then the youngest left for the Army, and the house went very quiet.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE QUIET HOUSE
segments.quote: When we are no longer able to change a situation, we are challenged to change ourselves.
segments.author: Viktor E. Frankl
lines: She cleaned the clean kitchen three times. Even the dog looked worried.
She wanted the boys back. That was not happening.
Then she remembered a line from Viktor Frankl, the Austrian doctor:
When we are no longer able to change a situation, we are challenged to change ourselves.
So she put down the sponge and opened the laptop.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE GAP
segments.quote: Above all, be the heroine of your life, not the victim.
segments.author: Nora Ephron
lines: Her resume had a hole the size of a moon crater.
Forty applications. Zero answers. She typed, I'm just a mom.
Her sister Gail texted her a line from the writer Nora Ephron:
Above all, be the heroine of your life, not the victim.
Renee rewrote it. Ran a five-person schedule for twenty-two years. Handled emergencies daily.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE INTERVIEW
segments.quote: If you can't make it better, you can laugh at it.
segments.author: Erma Bombeck
lines: Rocket City Plumbing called. The owner, Wanda Hicks, had a voice like a garbage disposal.
She asked, what's a P-trap? Renee's mind went blank. She said, a dance move?
Then she remembered Erma Bombeck, the humor writer:
If you can't make it better, you can laugh at it.
So Renee laughed. Wanda laughed harder. Renee got a one-week tryout.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE WRONG HOUSE
segments.quote: Isn't it nice to think that tomorrow is a new day with no mistakes in it yet?
segments.author: L. M. Montgomery
lines: Day three, she sent a plumber named Tiny, who is not tiny, to the wrong house.
The lady there gave him pie. Renee still drove home feeling awful.
She thought of Anne of Green Gables, by L. M. Montgomery:
Isn't it nice to think that tomorrow is a new day with no mistakes in it yet?
Next morning, she hung a big map and ran the trucks like a carpool. No more wrong houses.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE BIG FREEZE
segments.quote: These are the times that try men's souls.
segments.author: Thomas Paine
lines: In January, a hard freeze burst pipes all over town. Two hundred calls in one day.
Renee thought of her dad's favorite line, from Thomas Paine, the American patriot writer:
These are the times that try men's souls.
And women's, she said. She came in at five a.m. with a slow cooker of chili and kept every truck moving.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE OFFER
segments.quote: The only way to do great work is to love what you do.
segments.author: Steve Jobs
lines: In spring, Wanda offered her the office manager job.
Renee almost said, but I'm just a mom.
Then her son Marcus wrote from his base, quoting Steve Jobs, the Apple founder:
The only way to do great work is to love what you do.
She said yes. When Marcus came home on leave, he had to call dispatch to find his mother.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Change yourself. Own your story. Laugh. Start fresh. Step up. Love the work.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Change yourself. Be the hero. Laugh it off. Start fresh. Step up. Love what you do.
Me? I still think a P-trap is a dance move.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
